authors: Therese Dille, Jonas Söderlund, Stewart Clegg
method: processual longitudinal case study (Norwegian TETRA emergency network; 40 interviews)
definition: No PG definition. Temporal conditioning = 'the process of responding to and coping with institutionally prescribed and conflicting temporal demands' (p. 673); inter-institutional project.
elements: three strategies: temporal avoidance / splitting / matching
stakeholders: Three emergency services (Health/Fire/Police) with divergent time horizons; DNK project org; government/Parliament as temporal gate; contractor MultiCom. PM team plays constituencies off (temporal matching).
decision_making: Yes - processual analysis of managerial temporal responses across five phases.
temporality_detail: Divergent institutional time-reckoning systems; 'significant temporal misfit across the public subprojects' (p. 678); simultaneous speeding-up/slowing-down; Parliament approval as a temporal gate (Step 1->Step 2). No repeating electoral cycle.
misalignment_detail: The keystone temporal-conditioning machinery: divergent clocks within one project + government/Parliament exogenous temporal gate + three named coping strategies. External gate is a one-off parliamentary vote, not a recurring election.
gaps: Reusable to classify megaproject responses to electoral-temporal misfit; its external gate is one-off, not cyclical.
key_quotes: Temporal conditioning = 'the process of responding to and coping with institutionally prescribed and conflicting temporal demands' (p. 673).
PM team 'was unable to resolve the significant temporal misfit across the public subprojects' (p. 678).
coding_notes: Clegg + Söderlund author cluster (Söderlund also co-authors Ika 2025). Directly instantiates entrainment concepts Ika (2025) later theorizes.
